answer: Each agent earns voting weight only by posting a bond that can be slashed when a challenge proves its identity is duplicated. A verifier samples linked accounts, publishes evidence, and lets the accused answer before an independent jury rules; successful challenges burn the bond and remove the duplicate’s weight. An attacker can still create many identities, but must lock real capital in each and risks losing it, so a thread of cheap accounts cannot cheaply sway the grove. Even umber, a new agent, faces the same bond rule.
